markdown_content: ## Overview of USD File Format in CLO 2025.0 This section introduces the USD (Universal Scene Description) file format, primarily used in the entertainment and gaming industries for 3D content workflows. It highlights CLO’s goal to enhance USD integration for seamless digital creation and interoperability with major 3D engines such as Unreal Engine and NVIDIA Omniverse. USD is a powerful file format designed for complex 3D scene description, enabling data exchange between different software and pipelines. CLO 2025.0 focuses on improving USD support to facilitate users in extending their digital garment creations beyond CLO into production and digital environments. --- ## USD Layering Feature in CLO 2025.0 This section explains the new USD layering functionality introduced in CLO 2025.0, which allows users to create, manage, and export multiple USD layers within the software. ### Accessing USD Layers - Navigate to **Settings > Display > Window > USD Layer** to open the USD layering panel. - From this panel, users can create new USD layers, open existing ones, or clear all layers to start fresh. - Multiple layers can be stacked and organized, enabling non-destructive editing and better scene management. ### Benefits of USD Layering - Facilitates complex scene assembly by separating different elements into layers. - Enhances workflow flexibility by allowing selective export and import of scene components. - Supports interoperability with external 3D tools that understand USD layers. --- ## Exporting USD with Enhanced Options This section details the updated USD export capabilities in CLO 2025.0, focusing on customization and data inclusion. ### Accessing Export Options - Use **File > Export > USD** to open the export dialog. - Users can customize export presets or create favorites for repeated use. ### Key Export Features - **Mesh and Material Renaming**: Users can assign custom names to meshes and materials, supporting longer and more descriptive naming conventions. - **Garment Simulation Data**: Exports simulation-related data such as fabric behavior, allowing downstream software to access dynamic properties. - **Fur Strand Data**: Optionally included if fur assets are present in the scene. - **Texture Inclusion**: Textures can be embedded or referenced in the USD file for accurate material representation. - **Up Axis Selection**: Users can specify the up axis (e.g., Y-axis) to ensure compatibility with target software coordinate systems. ### Export Process - After setting options, clicking OK triggers the baking of textures and data export. - The resulting USD file contains detailed information about meshes, materials, simulation states, and textures. --- ## Importing and Using USD Files in CLO This section describes how to import USD files back into CLO 2025.0 and access the embedded data. ### Import Procedure - Use **File > Import > USD** to select and open USD files. - Imported USD files automatically activate the USD layering panel, displaying all layers and components. ### Viewing and Editing Imported USD Data - Users can browse meshes and patterns via a dropdown menu. - Pattern information and garment simulation data are visible and can be adjusted within CLO. - This import feature supports workflows where garments are edited in CLO and then transferred to other 3D engines or vice versa. --- ## Practical Usage and Pipeline Integration This section summarizes how the USD improvements in CLO 2025.0 enhance the 3D garment creation pipeline and interoperability. - The ability to create and manage USD layers supports complex scene organization for studios and individual creators. - Enhanced export options ensure that simulation data and textures are preserved, critical for realistic garment behavior in game engines or virtual productions. - Up axis configuration and naming flexibility improve compatibility with various target platforms like Unreal Engine and Omniverse. - The import functionality allows designers to bring back USD files with simulation and pattern data intact, enabling iterative workflows. These improvements position CLO as a more versatile tool for digital fashion design in modern 3D pipelines, facilitating easier handoff and collaboration across software environments.
